absent: PMU callback contracts for start, stop, pause handling and snapshot support beyond presence checks.
Group scheduling, rotation and multiplexing policy for pinned versus flexible queues.
Auxiliary compatibility predicate, auxiliary action detection and sample size negotiation.
Full layouts and lifetimes of event, context, processor context and buffer objects including mapped pages.
Clock arithmetic for context, processor and group time plus watermark and wakeup threshold selection.
Cross processor invocation mechanics, full locking hierarchy and tombstone task handling.
Numeric encodings for record types, header flags and sample masks plus userspace consumption protocol.
Deferred work handling after pending disable, wakeup and poll flags are set.

findings.text: Public disable operation acquires the event context, runs the internal disable path, then releases the context. It is the sleeping entry that may route work to the owning processor.

Local disable executes the disable handler on the current processor without cross processor routing. Deferred disable only marks a pending flag and enqueues asynchronous work so the actual disable happens later outside atomic context.

Output session start reserves space for a caller sized record and automatically selects forward or backward direction. Matching session end publishes the reservation and releases the read side critical section. A failed start means no session is open and nothing must be ended.

Header helpers prepare common record metadata and optionally handle an identifier trailer when all identifiers mode is enabled. One helper initializes in memory fields and size accounting, the other serializes the trailer into an already open handle.

Helper association is needed when redirection or an auxiliary action is requested. Establishment requires a leader, rejects combining redirection with sampled snapshots, checks leader compatibility for redirection plus capability presence for pause or snapshot support, and only links after safely acquiring a leader reference.

Helper teardown works in two directions. If the event points at a helper, that single link is cleared and one helper reference is dropped. If the event serves as helper, every sibling pointing at it is unlinked with one reference dropped per link, and each affected follower is scheduled out and moved to an erroneous condition that blocks further scheduling until explicitly reenabled.

Reference release drops the long count and returns while references remain. On the final drop it frees the event and then releases the parent link when present, so a parent outlives its children by exactly the hold taken at inheritance.

Group detachment clears membership exactly once and tolerates repeated calls. Departing members are unlinked with leader counts and generation adjusted, then promoted to standalone leaders with their own capabilities. Detaching a leader promotes every sibling to standalone while inheriting the former leader capabilities, clears the sibling count, and refreshes header sizes for all affected events.

Promotion to standalone reassigns leadership to self and installs the supplied capability set. Members that require group membership are first scheduled out and moved to an unrecoverable erroneous condition. Attached events rejoin context groups, running events rejoin the pinned or flexible active queue according to configuration, and header size is refreshed.

Child detachment clears membership once, warns when the expected parent link is missing, and unlinks from the parent collection. An event counts as orphaned exactly when its lifecycle has reached the terminal dead condition.
Eligibility filtering passes when processor assignment is wildcard or equals the current processor and group matching also passes.

Time handling updates the context clock on removal paths and the event clock on disable paths. Updates are skipped while frozen. Freezing first performs an update then marks frozen when time tracking is active. Event level update advances both context and group clocks.

Removal selects a lifecycle ceiling from caller flags, disables to at most that ceiling after time update, then optionally detaches group and child links and unlinks from the context. An emptied unit context clears rotation need and task association, while an emptied active context flushes group time for processor contexts then clears activity and task linkage.

Disable is a no operation for events already at or below off or inactive thresholds. Otherwise the unit is paused around time accounting, disabling a leader schedules out the whole group, but only the leader moves to off while members stay inactive.

Throttle and unthrottle act only on running events. Throttle saturates the interrupt counter, stops the unit, and emits a throttle marker for leaders. Unthrottle clears the counter, optionally restarts the unit, and emits an unthrottle marker for leaders.
Group throttle visits leader plus every sibling. Group unthrottle supports clearing all members while skipping restart of the triggering member.

Throttle markers carry the event clock, the primary identifier and the stream identifier, with a type distinguishing throttle from unthrottle. Emission is silently skipped when reservation fails. Trailer content follows the configured sample mask.

Identifier preparation copies the configured sample mask, records which identifier bits are present, and conditionally captures thread identity, clock, primary identifier, stream identifier and processor number. Serialization emits present fields in thread, time, identifier, stream, processor and extended identifier order.

Reservation redirects inherited events toward the parent, fails when no buffer is attached or when paused while counting a loss, prepends a loss marker with trailer overhead when losses are pending, checks circular space unless overwrite is allowed with direction aware roles, then atomically claims space and advances wakeup accounting when the watermark is crossed.
Total buffer bytes equal page count shifted by base page size plus an order value. One build configuration reads the order from the buffer, another fixes it at zero.

Group detachment requires the context lock held by the caller. Context removal requires the context mutex held, then uses the context spinlock for the fast inactive path and remote invocation otherwise.

Output sessions hold a read side critical section from successful reservation until matching end. Acquisition disables preemption, deepens a nesting count and snapshots wakeup progress. Outermost release publishes the head with ordering, retries when concurrent advance is detected, signals wakeup only on progress, and reenables preemption. Nested releases only unwind one level.
Throttle marker body holds a common header followed by an eight byte clock value, an eight byte primary identifier and an eight byte stream identifier.
Loss prefix body holds a common header followed by an eight byte identifier and an eight byte lost count.

Handle position is described by a page index from the claimed offset shifted by page size plus order and masked by page count minus one, plus a byte offset inside the page and the remaining span until the page end.

Event lifecycle includes off, inactive, active, error and terminal exit, revoked and dead conditions. Disable never raises state and clamps to the requested ceiling after scheduling out. Removal chooses the ceiling from flags. Helper loss and promotion of dependent members force error. Dead marks orphanhood.
Context activity records whether time flows and whether it is frozen. Active contexts accumulate time until frozen. Removing the last event clears activity and detaches task linkage.
Removal executes inline on the current processor when the context is inactive, otherwise it is routed to the owning processor. The path tolerates a tombstone task during exit.

Head publication can race with interrupt arrivals between nesting increment and head sampling. The outermost releaser validates the published value against the current head and retries on mismatch, so a stale value is never left permanently visible.
Missing buffer, paused state with storage, or insufficient circular space increments loss accounting on buffer and event and fails reservation without partial publication.

Backward mode claims space by moving the head in the opposite direction, swaps the roles of head and tail for space checks, and negates the value for publication math, so forward and backward accounting must stay distinct.
Detach selectors are single bit values with group one, child two, exit four, revoke eight and dead sixteen.
Saturated interrupt count has every bit set in an unsigned long long.

Wakeup signaling marks the buffer poll state readable, flags the event for deferred wakeup, conditionally arms deferred poll notification when asynchronous notification is configured, then enqueues deferred work.
